turns.question: I'm thinking of retiring at 58. Am I eligible, and how much would I get?
turns.answer:
**Calculated, with assumptions**

At age 58, you appear eligible under Section 11-134(a), because you have at least 20 years of service and the annuity can begin at age 55 or later. The estimate is **$32,126.78 annually**, or **$2,677.23 monthly**. The Code also gives you an election between formulas; the figure shown is the larger option on your numbers. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

Your record lists age 56, but you told me to use age 58 as the annuity-start age. This estimate rests on age 58.

| If you retire | Years of service | Annual pension | Monthly pension |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| at age 58 | 23.2 | $36,567.41 | $3,047.28 |

Waiting until age 58 is projected at **$36,567.41 annually**, or **$3,047.28 monthly**.



The difference is driven mainly by additional service and fewer months of reduction before age 60. Compared with the present estimate, the age-58 projection shows **$4,440.63** more annually and **$370.05** more monthly.

This projection holds your salary basis constant at today’s level and assumes continuous employment to that age.

**What I assumed**

- the date you stop working, taken as today

Section 11-134(a) applies because you have at least 20 years of service and the annuity may begin at age 55 or later. Its early-retirement provision reduces the annuity by **0.25% for each full month or fractional part thereof** that the annuity begins before age 60. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The Code lets you elect the tiered formula of **1.80%**, **2.00%**, **2.20%**, and **2.40%** for successive service periods instead of another annuity under Section 11-134(a); the figure shown is the larger option on your numbers. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The election under Section 11-134(f-1) does not apply because it requires the annuity to begin no earlier than age 60. The age-and-service annuity under Section 11-130 does apply, but the Code does not contain the accumulated-contribution conversion factors needed to put a figure on it. Section 11-131 does not apply because it concerns withdrawal before age 55 followed by attainment of age 55. Section 11-164(1) does not apply because it concerns refunds in specified cases involving withdrawal before age 55 or fewer than 10 years of service.

This is an estimate — your retirement fund makes the binding determination.

turns.question: what does Article 4 provide for police officers?
turns.answer:
Article 4 provides firefighter pensions, not police officer pensions. It covers firefighters of municipalities and includes retirement, disability, survivor, and related benefits. [40 ILCS 5/4-108] [40 ILCS 5/4-110]

- A firefighter’s creditable service is generally time served as a municipal firefighter, subject to the Code’s rules for leaves and certain other eligible service. [40 ILCS 5/4-108]
- Article 4 includes line-of-duty disability pensions when a firefighter is permanently disabled because of an act of duty or its cumulative effects. [40 ILCS 5/4-110]
- The Article 4 fund has exclusive authority to decide and award benefits under Article 4. [40 ILCS 5/4-117.2]

Your own pension comes under Article 11, according to your record. This answer does not determine or calculate your pension under Article 11. A dollar figure would require the applicable Article 11 benefit provision and the figures needed under that provision.
